correctness.rationale: The gap SDE is a strictly contractive PDMP with three-state independent sign-flip generator and invariant compact interval. Mode-resolved forward fluxes and vanishing boundary currents yield exact integrated relations; near each edge, two nondominant mode masses are smaller by one and two powers of strip width, respectively. Integrating the attracting-mode logarithmic derivative gives a finite positive coefficient, power exponent 2 gamma/h, and controlled density remainder. The exact roots and slopes produce the strict phase classification and boundary cases. Verified full-generator sparse finite-volume calculations at four rates in the packaged checker corroborate without constituting the proof.

A generic PDMP edge theorem or a specialization of the 2021 broad ODE is a genuine residual priority risk, so this is a best-knowledge self-review originality judgment, not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Nearest-neighbor gap is a natural structural observable in an interacting active-gas model. Different edge exponents and two sharp tumbling thresholds distinguish near-contact and maximal-separation probabilities and identify a nonempty regime with a divergent small-gap density but a vanishing large-gap density. These statistics are not supplied by one-point particle-density edge exponents or by a mere numerical table, and the result applies across the full four-positive-parameter model.
